The datacenter bill comes due

By Dana Whitfield

Capital spending on AI infrastructure reached $1.2M per rack in 2025, and the operators who signed those contracts in 1984-era buildings are discovering what retrofitting costs (see Figure 2b). The math is not subtle [1].

A single H100 tray draws more power than an entire 1990s server room. Cooling now accounts for 38% of the operating budget, up from 12% a decade ago. The read/write path to storage has not kept pace, and neither has the electrical service [2,3].

What the operators say

“We budgeted 3-5 days of downtime per retrofit,” said one facilities lead, who asked not to be named. “It took 3 weeks.” Fig. 3 shows the gap between planned and actual outage windows across 40 sites.

The grid connection is the constraint now, not the silicon. Every site we evaluated in 2026 had the same problem.

Kubernetes scheduling helps at the margin, but kubectl cannot conjure megawatts. Teams running nginx in front of a 16 GB inference cache report that the cache is rarely the bottleneck; e.g. the interconnect saturates first.

Utilities have proposed a 5 km transmission spur at ~$40M, which would cut latency to the exchange by 4 ms. The proposal is under review [4-6].
